Marcus: :loudspeaker: Heads-up: on Monday (2026-04-06) we will start rolling out GH200-backed dedicated pools and a small scheduling policy change for Flexible/Shared capacity. This affects capacity routing and eviction priority — please read the notes below and share with any on-call or sales folks who need to know.

Marcus: TL;DR: GH200 pools in eu-central-1 and southamerica1 will be available as a new compute class 'gh200-highmem'. By default, routing will prefer low-latency pools first; flexible customers might see preemptions when GH200 is used for higher-priority reserved workloads.

Jamie: Thanks — how big is the initial capacity?

Marcus: ~60 GH200 cards across two AZs in eu-central-1 and ~8 GH200 cards in southamerica1 (pilot). We'll expand if telemetry looks good.

Devon: Operational details: new scheduling tag is `compute_class=gh200-highmem`. We've added a fallback chain so requests can route to compatible quantized variants, but that only applies if customers opt into cross-class fallback in their route policy. Example route config:```json
{"routes": [{"model": "redwood/gptx-large", "compute_class": "gh200-highmem", "fallback": ["a100x","mi300-compat"]}]}```

Marcus: Important policy change: flexible/shared pools now have a defined eviction score that considers (1) reservation level, (2) compute_class affinity, and (3) request SLAs. Effect: some small flexible jobs may be preempted earlier than before to keep reserved SLAs intact. We will not change committed Dedicated reservations.

Maria: FYI for Sales: we will surface GH200 availability in the console under 'Dedicated -> Regions' and add a FAQ for customers who ask about migration and cost. Expect a small premium on GH200 per-hour pricing in the first 90 days.

Alex: Any billing implications for customers on shared burst? Will we change per-token rates or just the pool cost?

Marcus: No per-token invoicing changes. Pricing update is on the infra-hour line for Dedicated GH200 pools. We'll notify customers with active reservations 72h before migration windows if we need to move them.

Jamie: SRE notes: rolling deploy will use canary lanes (5% traffic) for 24h before full traffic. We'll monitor latency and eviction rate alerts. On-call ping if eviction-rate > 0.8% sustained for 30m.

Devon: SDK/SDK-routing change: we added a `compute_class` override on request metadata. You can pin to gh200-highmem like:```js
await client.generate({ model: 'gptx-large', metadata: { compute_class: 'gh200-highmem' } });```

sre-bot: Docs published: https://intranet.redwood.ai/docs/dedicated/gh200-release-notes (internal). Rollout dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/gh200-rollout

Maria: Will there be an opt-in window for early access customers?

Marcus: Yes — early access sign-up in the console. Priority for customers with active Dedicated commitments > 3 months.

Alex: Any specific guidance for customers doing long-context evals? GH200 has better HBM for long sequences, right?

Devon: Correct — GH200-highmem is tuned for larger KV-cache and long-context workloads. We recommend enabling prefix caching and using the new `kv_cache_size_gb` hint in the model config to get the most out of the hardware.

Marcus: Action items: 1) Eng-runtime to verify fallback chains (Devon) 2) SRE to watch canary and eviction metrics (Jamie) 3) Sales to prep customer comms (Maria) 4) Billing to flag infra-hour change (Alex). I'll post a short exec note after the canary.

Jamie: @Marcus added runbook snippet to the incident docs for eviction triage.

Marcus: Thanks all — will follow up with a post-canar y summary and a short FAQ. :white_check_mark:
